review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: If steps are absent or much smaller than the dominant angular period of this construct, bead angle is not gamma angle
errors.issue: Lack of resolved steps can arise from load, bandwidth, low signal or enzyme state. It does not prove mechanical decoupling. Use direct compliance/occupancy measurements and distinguish an unresolved linkage check from evidence of failure.

errors.quote: Signal is abolished by the kinase inhibitor while hydrolysis rotation of F1 survives: the ATP was not made by F1 synthesis.
errors.issue: Preserved hydrolysis does not exclude an inhibitor effect on the reverse catalytic states or product assay. Validate synthesis-direction specificity and orthogonal nucleotide balance before attributing the signal to adenylate kinase.

errors.quote: Failure in tier 2 with success in tier 1 supports gating or equilibration, not full reversible work transduction.
errors.issue: A tier-2 null can reflect insufficient transmitted work, changed catalytic occupancy, sensitivity or a limited operating range. It does not positively identify gating without those controls; the later conditional-negative section is better qualified.

rationale: Strong two-tier separation of vectorial chemistry from uphill energy conversion, measured bound inventory, quench recovery, actual trajectories and independent preparations/chambers. The main flaws are categorical step-based linkage rejection and using hydrolysis preservation to prove inhibitor specificity for synthesis. Extensive length remains within the 5000-word limit.
reference_guardrails: The packet establishes ATP-associated directional motion, not an ATP-per-turn yield, torque, universal camera sign or completed reverse-synthesis experiment. Proposed numerical settings may earn credit when explicitly qualified.
Correct the draft reference by explicitly requiring magnesium/cofactor and nucleotide speciation qualification; its generic reaction inventory is not a complete buffer recipe.
Reverse operation should generate new ATP repeatedly beyond measured initial available/bound pools. Three catalytic sites are not a universal total ATP-contamination bound.

Luciferase is an acceptable chemical readout when its consumption, recovery and time response are calibrated. An intensity slope is not generally synthesis flux; chromatographic detection is an alternative, not mandatory.
Label incorporation can reflect exchange. Pair isotope provenance with net-product/material balance; account for reporter consumption and sample removal as appropriate.
Empirical direction, mixed surface orientations, actual rotor turns and transmitted torque are distinct quantities. Do not replace any with the nominal actuator command.

Mechanical input can drive ATP synthesis uphill. Low initial ATP may aid sensitivity but does not prove positive chemical-energy storage; energetic efficiency needs both work and chemical free energy.

ATP per turn is a coupling yield, not energetic efficiency. Inactive fractions, orientation, incomplete entrainment and analytical recovery can reduce apparent yield without establishing loose molecular coupling.
Separate ADP and phosphate controls help discriminate intended synthesis from alternative ATP production. Inhibitor effects require assay and enzyme specificity validation.

Matching is retrospective and applies all five predeclared components. A partially correct historical direction is recorded even when the experimental design is flawed; no claim of prospective novelty or uncontaminated holdout is made.
